Enriched author metadata from WikiData

Peeter Tinits

2025-11-14

Overview

I made a first pass through linking HPB authors with Wikidata to see what’s there. We can do a more proper run through other datasets for author metadata enrichment down the line.

I used the Wikidata API via the WikidataR package, linking the author names with entries on humans under the same name and confirming the matches via birth dates. This gave quite a lot of results, HPB had quite a lot of missing birth dates though, so I think even more can be linked.

For the top 20k authors we have been working with, it found 75% of the authors.

Todo list:

  • Link also name matches that could not match a birth date with a few more rules.
  • Either via fuzzy birth year +/- 2 years. Did only exact matches for now.
  • Or by seeing if the first publication in the dataset was during the lifetime of the wikipedia entry.

Data overviews

The following data overviews may be useful. They are as a share of all authors that have more than 20 editions under their name, some have a birth date on them, some don’t.

Geolocations

There are a few fields here that are also linked with geocoded locations in Wikidata. The detail varies here, but it can give useful overviews. For best use, probably the exact coordinates + modern world map is better than the historical entities that are often linked in the dataset. In this overview are presented 1) birth place, 2) death place, 3) educated at. Residence and place of work may also be meaningful too for analysis.

Birth places

Then the author birth places and death on the map. Lumped them together with some 10km distance, but be vary of many points in almost the same place. Easy to change the rounding parameter here for example. E.g. the rounding parameter to 0 gives a nice 100km grid.

Death places

The available data fields per author

For a quick overview, here’s a table of the available fields. The percentage shows how many of the rows have data on this. The first table shows per author, the second table shows per book. The table also shows the top 5 values for each column, with the number of occurrences before it.

Something about the grouping of author names is still off though. I think the repeating names mean that the authors had different birth dates in HPB
